text:
Ryan McLeod has four points in 19 games, and Buffalo is winless in his last four games, so it's fair to ask what happened. A lot of it is luck. The Sabres have scored 10.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with McLeod on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league, and he's shooting 6.2% on a talent range around 13%. His scoring rate, 0.85 points per 60, is less than half of what we'd expect from him.

Not all of it is bounces. He plays 14:49 a night, down more than a minute over his last 10, and his own chances are thin (0.41 expected goals per 60, down from 0.50). He's never been a shooter: NHL Edge has his top shot speed in the 16th percentile, while his skating sits in the 98th. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 8.0 primary shot assists per 60, and Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.9 wins, though with a warning that his results ran well ahead of his chances. The Buffalo News noted this week that he's closing in on an NHL milestone.
